newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn, Buba near deal to revalue reserves - sources.
newsitem.headline: Bonn, Buba near deal to revalue reserves - sources.

text.p: The German government and the Bundesbank are near a deal to revalue the central bank's dollar reserves at 1.50 marks or higher, up from 1.3620 marks currently, government sources said on Tuesday.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel, who will discuss the pact again this week with Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer, is counting on getting about 10 billion marks in 1998 from the revaluation of the dollar reserves, the sources said.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition hopes to use the funds to retire old debt. It will not help relieve the budget deficit crunch, but it could help Germany meet the deficit target for European monetary union, the sources said.
Unlike gold reserves, the revaluation of the dollar reserves can be decided by the central bank council, and does not require a change in the law.
The government and the central bank are apparently still talking about whether to revalue the gold reserves and when, after Waigel backed down from an earlier plan to revalue them this year.
